sections.title: Immediate help and suicide safety
sections.body_markdown:
- **Immediate danger, overdose, serious injury, or inability to stay safe:** Call 911 or seek emergency care. Do not wait for a professional-assistance callback. ([AANA help resources](https://www.aana.com/membership/here-for-you/health-and-wellness/where-to-get-help/))
- **Suicidal thoughts or emotional distress:** In the United States, call or text 988, or use the 988 website chat, any time. You can also contact 988 because you are worried about someone else. ([988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline](https://988lifeline.org/))
- **Reach a person:** Tell a trusted person that you need support and ask them to stay with you while you connect with care; reduce access to medications, weapons, and other dangerous items when it can be done safely. ([988 guidance](https://988lifeline.org/help-someone-else/))
- **Outside the United States:** Use your local emergency number or local crisis service. These contact listings are U.S.-focused.
- **Luma is a reference, not a monitored service:** This page does not dispatch help, monitor your safety, or provide counseling. Use the listed services directly.

sections.title: AANA, ASA, and national support
sections.body_markdown:
- **AANA Helpline: 800-654-5167.** Available 24/7 for confidential support, information, and resources for CRNAs and nurse anesthesia residents with drug or alcohol concerns; colleagues, administrators, friends, and family can also call with concerns. It is not a substitute for 911 or 988 in an immediate crisis. ([AANA help resources](https://www.aana.com/membership/here-for-you/health-and-wellness/where-to-get-help/), [AANA substance-use resources](https://www.aana.com/membership/here-for-you/health-and-wellness/substance-use-disorder-sud/))
- **ASA well-being resources:** ASA links to 988, Physician Support Line, professional-health programs, and other support options. These are distinct services, not one ASA-operated crisis hotline. ([ASA well-being](https://www.asahq.org/advocating-for-you/well-being))
- **Physician Support Line: 888-409-0141.** Free, confidential, anonymous peer support from volunteer psychiatrists for U.S. physicians and medical students; Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–11 p.m. Eastern, excluding federal holidays. No appointment needed; not a 24/7 emergency line and not a service advertised for all license types. ([Physician Support Line](https://www.physiciansupportline.com/))
- **ASA Member Services: 630-912-2552.** Administrative contact for membership and resource questions; Monday–Friday, 7:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m. Central. This is not a crisis, counseling, or treatment line. ([ASA Member Experience FAQs](https://www.asahq.org/member-center/membership-faqs), [ASA published contact hours](https://www.asahq.org/about-asa/asa-refund-policy))
- **ASA SafeHaven:** Check current enrollment and benefit availability directly with ASA. The public offer page reviewed for this resource still describes benefit access ending November 30, 2025; do not assume its older price or access terms remain valid. ([ASA SafeHaven](https://www.asahq.org/advocating-for-you/safehaven))
- **SAMHSA treatment referral: 800-662-4357.** Free, confidential, 24/7 information and treatment-referral service in English and Spanish for mental-health and substance-use concerns. This service does not provide counseling. ([SAMHSA National Helpline](https://www.samhsa.gov/find-help/national-helpline))

sections.title: If you are struggling during clinical work
sections.body_markdown:
- **Put immediate safety first:** If you may be unable to provide safe care, arrange a safe handoff and notify the appropriate clinical supervisor or designated fitness-for-duty contact. Protect both patients and the provider; do not manage the concern alone. ([AANA substance-use and workplace guidance](https://www.aana.com/membership/here-for-you/health-and-wellness/substance-use-disorder-sud/))
- **Ask for assessment rather than diagnosing yourself:** Contact a qualified mental-health or addiction clinician, your available employee-assistance service, or an appropriate professional-assistance program. PHPs can help coordinate evaluation, treatment, and continuing-care monitoring; they do not replace an emergency department. ([AANA help resources](https://www.aana.com/membership/here-for-you/health-and-wellness/where-to-get-help/), [FSPHP FAQs](https://www.fsphp.org/faqs))
- **Burnout, grief, and depression deserve attention:** Sleep difficulty, appetite changes, and depression can accompany sustained professional stress; connect with professional support rather than treating all distress as something to push through. ([ASA well-being](https://www.asahq.org/advocating-for-you/well-being))
- **After an adverse event:** Ask about your institution's peer-support service and professional counseling options. Peer support and follow-up are resources for recovery, not proof that you are unfit to practice. ([ASA well-being resources](https://www.asahq.org/advocating-for-you/well-being))
- **Withdrawal needs clinical assessment:** Ask a qualified clinician what level of care is safe; a working-professionals program is not automatically a medical detox unit. Parkdale's program page specifically distinguishes withdrawal management from detoxification services. ([Parkdale program descriptions](https://parkdalecenter.com/programs/))

sections.title: Helping a colleague
sections.body_markdown:
- **Ask directly and kindly:** “I am concerned about you. Are you thinking about suicide?” Listen without judgment; do not argue, shame, or offer simplistic reassurance. ([988 guidance](https://988lifeline.org/help-someone-else/))
- **Connect, do not promise secrecy:** If a colleague describes a plan to hurt themselves, seek crisis support rather than agreeing to keep it secret; call 988 for guidance or 911 for immediate danger. ([988 guidance](https://988lifeline.org/help-someone-else/), [AANA crisis resources](https://www.aana.com/membership/here-for-you/health-and-wellness/where-to-get-help/))
- **Use the proper workplace channel:** Concerning behavior or suspected diversion should be addressed through the supervisor or designated chain of command, with provider and patient safety as priorities. AANA can advise on addressing a substance-use concern safely. ([AANA substance-use resources](https://www.aana.com/membership/here-for-you/health-and-wellness/substance-use-disorder-sud/))
- **Do not diagnose from a single behavior:** Absences, personality changes, or documentation concerns are not by themselves proof of substance misuse. Seek appropriate assessment rather than labeling a colleague. ([Marworth healthcare-professional guidance](https://www.marworth.org/programs/healthcare-professionals))
- **Follow up:** Stay connected after the immediate conversation and help the person reach ongoing support. Take care of your own well-being when supporting someone in distress. ([988 guidance](https://988lifeline.org/help-someone-else/))

sections.title: Choosing treatment and planning recovery
sections.body_markdown:
- **Match the program to your needs:** Ask whether the program treats your profession, mental-health concerns, substance-use condition, and any needed withdrawal or medical stabilization. Healthcare-professional programs describe different evaluation, treatment, and re-entry services. ([Marworth](https://www.marworth.org/programs/healthcare-professionals), [Parkdale](https://parkdalecenter.com/programs/), [Talbott](https://talbottcampus.com/addiction-treatment-programs/professionals/healthcare-professionals-program/))
- **Clarify professional requirements before enrollment when safe to do so:** Ask the relevant assistance or monitoring program whether a proposed evaluation or treatment provider meets its requirements. Do not delay emergency care to obtain administrative approval. ([FSPHP FAQs](https://www.fsphp.org/faqs))
- **Ask about practical details:** Confirm intake availability, level of care, cost, insurance, travel, co-occurring-condition care, family involvement, medication treatment options, and continuing care directly with the facility; inclusion here is not a guarantee of availability or coverage.
- **Return to practice is individualized:** Work with the treating team and, when applicable, employer, credentialing body, licensing board, and monitoring program. Completion of a treatment program does not by itself guarantee unrestricted return to anesthesia practice. ([FSPHP FAQs](https://www.fsphp.org/faqs), [AANA workplace guidance](https://www.aana.com/membership/here-for-you/health-and-wellness/substance-use-disorder-sud/))
- **Recovery community:** AANA describes Anesthetists in Recovery (AIR), an independent virtual community for CRNAs and nurse anesthesia residents in or seeking recovery; use AANA's page for current contact information. Peer support complements, rather than replaces, indicated treatment. ([AANA recovery resources](https://www.aana.com/membership/here-for-you/health-and-wellness/substance-use-disorder-sud/))

sections.title: Confidentiality, reporting, and what to ask
sections.body_markdown:
- **Ask about limits before sharing nonurgent identifying details:** “Who can access my information? What triggers disclosure or a board report? Is this voluntary treatment, peer support, or formal monitoring?” Program structure and legal requirements vary; no directory can promise anonymity or no licensing consequences across all states and professions. ([FSPHP FAQs](https://www.fsphp.org/faqs), [AANA reporting guidance](https://www.aana.com/membership/here-for-you/health-and-wellness/substance-use-disorder-sud/))
- **Separate the services:** An association helpline, a treating clinician, a PHP, a nursing assistance program, and a licensing board are not interchangeable. Confirm eligibility and the role of the service you contact. ([FSPHP state-program directory](https://www.fsphp.org/state-programs), [AANA help resources](https://www.aana.com/membership/here-for-you/health-and-wellness/where-to-get-help/))
- **PHP has two meanings:** In the state directory it means Physician/Professional Health Program; in a treatment facility's description it can mean partial hospitalization program. Do not confuse a monitoring/referral service with a level of treatment. ([FSPHP FAQs](https://www.fsphp.org/faqs), [Parkdale programs](https://parkdalecenter.com/programs/))
- **Emergency exception:** Questions about privacy or employment should not delay emergency help when someone is in immediate danger. ([AANA crisis resources](https://www.aana.com/membership/here-for-you/health-and-wellness/where-to-get-help/))

sections.title: Directory scope and verification
sections.body_markdown:
- **State resources:** The selector covers all 50 states and Washington, D.C. Most entries are professional-health assistance, evaluation-coordination, or monitoring contacts, not treatment facilities; eligibility for CRNAs, CAAs, physicians, and trainees must be checked with the individual program. ([FSPHP directory](https://www.fsphp.org/state-programs))
- **Nurse anesthesia route in every state:** AANA's national helpline can provide CRNA- and nurse-anesthesia-resident-focused substance-use support and help identify relevant resources. A physician-only program should not be presumed to accept nurses. ([AANA](https://www.aana.com/membership/here-for-you/health-and-wellness/where-to-get-help/))
- **Treatment facilities:** The separate list is a selected, non-ranked set of programs with publicly described professional tracks, not an exhaustive all-state rehab directory and not an endorsement.
- **Source checks:** Public source pages were checked September 26, 2026. Telephone connections, bed availability, insurance participation, and each program's current eligibility were not confirmed by phone; verify these directly.
- **Privacy in this screen:** Luma does not ask you to enter symptoms, substance use, licensing details, or a personal history here. The state selection stays on this screen; external sites and calls have their own privacy practices.

facilities.name: Parkdale Center
facilities.body: Working-professionals addiction treatment with partial hospitalization, intensive outpatient, dual-diagnosis care, and career-restoration support. AANA identifies its Parkdale partnership for CRNAs and nurse anesthesia residents. Confirm your required level of care: Parkdale's program page distinguishes withdrawal management from medical detoxification.

facilities.name: Geisinger Marworth
facilities.body: Healthcare Professionals Program with professional peer groups, re-entry planning, co-occurring-condition care, recurrence-prevention support, medication-assisted treatment, and withdrawal/detox help. The published contact is available 24/7; ask admissions to confirm the appropriate evaluation and level of care.

facilities.name: Talbott Recovery
facilities.body: Atlanta Healthcare Professionals Program describes multidisciplinary evaluation, addiction and co-occurring psychiatric care, partial hospitalization with recovery residences, continuing care, and professional re-entry support. Confirm the appropriate campus and current services with admissions.

facilities.name: Bradford at Warrior
facilities.body: Healthcare Professionals Program for licensed professionals, including physicians and nurses, with evaluation, substance-use treatment, co-occurring-condition care, and return-to-practice support. The facility publishes a 24/7 general contact; evaluation appointments are listed separately at 205-756-3503.
